blogs.title: Neck Swelling Without Infection: Recognizing Pseudo‑Angioedema as a Manifestation of Dermatomyositis
blogs.description: This post dissects the rare presentation of inflammatory myopathy as non‑histaminergic neck edema that mimics Ludwig’s angina or idiopathic angioedema. It highlights red‑flag features—persistent swelling despite antibiotics, lack of fever or airway compromise, subtle peri‑ungual changes—and outlines a rapid bedside work‑up (creatine kinase, nailfold capillaroscopy, skin exam) that can pivot the diagnosis toward dermatomyositis before invasive ENT interventions.

blogs.title: Anti‑SAE1 Antibodies Unveiled: Clinical Phenotype, Prognosis and Malignancy Risk
blogs.description: Focusing on the small ubiquitin‑like modifier activating enzyme‑1 autoantibody, this article reviews the emerging data linking anti‑SAE1 positivity with distinctive cutaneous findings (holster sign, periungual erythema), high rates of dysphagia and interstitial lung disease, and an intermediate‑to‑high malignancy risk profile. Practical guidance is provided on when to order comprehensive myositis panels and how to interpret SAE‑related serologies within a broader diagnostic algorithm.

blogs.title: When ENT Meets Immunology: A Multidisciplinary Algorithm for Unexplained Deep Neck Space Swelling
blogs.description: Using the case as a framework, this entry walks readers through a stepwise pathway that integrates ENT imaging (CT/airway assessment), infectious work‑up (CBC/CRP/aspiration cultures), complement studies for hereditary/acquired angioedema, and early rheumatologic input (CK measurement, autoantibody panels). The goal is to provide an actionable flowchart that reduces diagnostic delay and avoids unnecessary surgical exploration.

blogs.title: Beyond Steroids: Tailoring Immunosuppression for Severe Dermatomyositis With Airway Involvement
blogs.description: The article reviews evidence‑based strategies for managing aggressive DM presenting with cervical muscle edema and dysphagia. It covers pulse methylprednisolone protocols, indications for early IVIG loading doses, rational use of rituximab versus traditional steroid‑sparing agents, and why mycophenolate mofetil was favored over methotrexate in a patient with subclinical lung disease. Prophylactic measures such as PJP prophylaxis and monitoring for treatment toxicity are also discussed.

blogs.title: Cancer Surveillance in Dermatomyositis: Applying IMACS Guidelines to Anti‑SAE1 Positive Patients
blogs.description: This post translates IMACS cancer‑screening recommendations into practical steps for clinicians caring for DM patients with high‑risk features—anti‑SAE1 positivity, dysphagia, male sex—and outlines a tiered imaging schedule (baseline CT chest/abdomen/pelvis, FDG‑PET when indicated) combined with age‑appropriate endoscopic evaluations. It also addresses follow‑up intervals, red flag symptoms prompting re‑evaluation, and balancing thoroughness against resource utilization.
